bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: speed up integer and mixed integer/double arithmetic loops

comments.text:
Integer and mixed integer/double arithmetic can avoid per-element recycling
bookkeeping when the operands have equal lengths or one operand is a scalar.
This patch extends the loop specialization already used for double arithmetic
and factors the dispatch into a shared macro. Numerical results and warning
behavior are preserved.

Reproducible example (CPU seconds; run in the original and patched builds):

invisible(compiler::enableJIT(0))
set.seed(20261113)
x <- sample.int(10L, 100000L, replace = TRUE)
y <- sample.int(5L, 100000L, replace = TRUE)
run <- compiler::cmpfun(function(x, y, n) {
    for (i in seq_len(n)) z <- x + y
    z
})
bench <- function(x, y) {
    invisible(run(x, y, 10L))
    gc()
    t0 <- proc.time()
    invisible(run(x, y, 1000L))
    dt <- proc.time() - t0
    unname(dt["user.self"] + dt["sys.self"])
}
c(integer_add = bench(x, y), mixed_add = bench(x, y + 0.5))

The example processes 100 million elements in each case. In five interleaved
runs of the fuller benchmark using these inputs on ARM64 macOS, Apple Clang
21, and -std=gnu23 -g -O2, median CPU times were:

Equal-length operands        Original (ms)   Patched (ms)
integer + integer                     153            105
integer - integer                     115             72
integer * integer                      98             64
integer / integer                      80             40
integer %/% integer                    95             38
integer + double                       78             19

Timings include allocation and garbage collection. The expected improvement is
lower runtime with the same values, types, NA propagation, and overflow
warnings. These measurements are from one compiler/architecture and are not a
guarantee of gains elsewhere.

Analysis:

In src/main/arithmetic.c, integer_binary() and the mixed-type paths in
real_binary() commonly use MOD_ITERATE2_CHECK even for scalar or equal-length
operands. BINARY_ITERATE2_CHECK in src/include/R_ext/Itermacros.h dispatches
those cases to R_ITERATE_CHECK, loads a scalar operand once, and retains
MOD_ITERATE2_CHECK for general recycling. Callers supply two typed operand
declarations and one operation body.

The helper is used for all integer binary arithmetic, mixed integer/double +,
-, *, and /, and the existing double/double +, -, *, /, and ^ fast paths. It
retains the original arithmetic/overflow helpers and interrupt intervals and
needs no new compiler feature check. Replacing only the handwritten
multiplication dispatch with the macro produces identical optimized Clang
assembly.

There is a measured tradeoff: two mixed integer/double %/% cases became slower
despite unchanged source loops. Separate five-round measurements of 300
million elements showed 728 -> 791 ms for a scalar RHS and 819 -> 916 ms for a
recycled length-16 RHS (8.7% and 11.8% slower); the broader sweep measured up
to about 16% for the latter. The cause has not been established.
Floating-point %% and %/%, and mixed-type powers, retain their generic loops
after uneven results in the wider experiment.

Validation:

- The full test-Reg target and arith.R, arith-true.R, and iec60559.R passed (build configured without recommended packages).
- 18,060 differential cases matched the original, including interpreted and compiled evaluation, NA/NaN/Inf, signed zeros, warnings, attributes, aliasing, empty vectors, and recycling. Large-vector checks crossed the interrupt boundary.
- A C harness passed 2,197 length/interrupt-interval combinations and scalar/output aliasing checks with Clang 21, GCC 16, and Clang ASan/UBSan.

Proposed patch: attached as binary-arithmetic-loops.diff. It includes
regression tests and applies with patch -p0 against SVN r90887; a dry run with
zero fuzz passed. Benchmarks and regression testing used the r90883 base, and
the three touched files are unchanged between r90883 and r90887.

This is complementary to bug 19096
(https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19096), which discusses changing
overflow checks. This patch preserves those checks.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/486,
where the full benchmark results, review discussion, and CI results can be
seen.

comments.text:
Created attachment 4054
patch: share and specialize binary arithmetic loop dispatch

Created attachment 4055
patch: share and specialize binary arithmetic loop dispatch (portable tests)

I have updated the patch to make the new arithmetic regression test portable.
Combining NA and NaN may produce either missing value, as documented in ?NA.
The scalar-reference test required the same choice for scalar and vector
operations; that assertion also fails with the original arithmetic code on
x86 Linux. The test now permits this specific difference while continuing to
check missingness, all other values, and signed zeros exactly. The integer
NA and overflow-warning checks are unchanged.

I also removed unnecessary braces from single-statement macro invocations.
The corrected regression blocks pass with Clang and GCC on x86 Linux, and
the native ARM64 test-Reg and arithmetic tests pass. This attachment replaces
4054 and applies with patch -p0 against SVN r90887 (zero-fuzz dry run passed).

The updated patch and CI results are also at
https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/486.
